name: Indonesia: Java highlands + Tana Toraja
tagline: Borobudur at dawn, temples older than Angkor on a 2,100 m plateau, volcanoes, then the highlands of Sulawesi in funeral season.

access.route: Brussels→Yogyakarta via Doha, Singapore or Kuala Lumpur (16–18 h); Makassar by internal flight

nightsNote: 8–12°C at Dieng and Bromo, 18°C in Toraja, 24°C in Yogyakarta
whyNotes: Dry season, cheap on the ground, and a culture none of you has seen: 8th-century Buddhist and Hindu Java, then Toraja, where July and August are the season of the great funeral ceremonies and the village trekking is at 1,300–1,600 m and 24°C.
fitNotes: Altitude trivial (2,400 m max at the volcano rims). Heat is the limit: Yogyakarta and Makassar are 31°C and humid, so the city days are short and the highland days long. Borobudur and Bromo are crowded at sunrise; Dieng and Toraja are not. Long flights (16+ h) and an internal hop.

blocks.name: Yogyakarta
blocks.place: Borobudur, Prambanan, the Kraton, batik, Malioboro
blocks.history: 8th–9th-century Buddhist and Hindu kingdoms, Javanese sultanate
see: Borobudur at sunrise (limited climbing tickets, book ahead)
Prambanan late afternoon and the Ramayana ballet
Kraton and Taman Sari water castle
Batik workshop in Kota Gede
Ratu Boko at sunset
blocks.note: Hot and busy; do the sites at opening and the city after 4 pm.

blocks.name: Solo (Surakarta)
blocks.place: Two keratons, gamelan, the quieter Javanese court city
see: Mangkunegaran palace and its gamelan
Pasar Triwindu antiques market
Sangiran early-man museum (UNESCO)

blocks.name: Malang + Batu
blocks.place: Dutch colonial hill city at 450–1,000 m, apple orchards, temples
see: Jodipan rainbow village and the colonial quarter
Singosari and Jago temples
Coban Rondo waterfall

blocks.name: Makassar
blocks.place: Fort Rotterdam, Bugis schooners at Paotere, seafood
see: Fort Rotterdam and the La Galigo museum
Paotere harbour pinisi schooners
Rammang-Rammang karst by boat (half day)
blocks.note: Internal flight from Yogyakarta or Surabaya. Hot; one night.

blocks.name: Tana Toraja: Rantepao
blocks.place: Tongkonan houses, cliff graves at Lemo and Londa, Kete Kesu, funeral ceremonies
blocks.history: Toraja ancestor culture, Aluk To Dolo
see: A funeral ceremony with a local guide (July–August is the season; guests bring a gift)
Londa and Lemo cliff graves, tau-tau effigies
Kete Kesu village and rice barns
Bolu buffalo market (every six days)
blocks.note: 8 h by road from Makassar, or the 1 h flight to Toraja airport when it runs. Cool, green, unhurried.

blocks.name: Toraja highland trekking
blocks.place: Batutumonga, Lolai, Baruppu: rice terraces and villages at 1,300–1,600 m
see: Batutumonga ridge walk above the valley
Village-to-village day stages with homestays
Lolai 'land above the clouds' at dawn
Bori Parinding megaliths

blocks.name: Dieng plateau
blocks.place: 2,100 m volcanic plateau, Java's oldest temples, Sikunir sunrise, coloured lakes
blocks.history: 7th–8th-century Hindu temples, the oldest on Java
see: Arjuna temple complex in the mist
Sikunir hill sunrise over the volcanoes
Telaga Warna lakes and Sikidang crater
Potato-farm villages, cold nights
blocks.note: Cool, cheap, almost no foreign visitors. 3 h from Yogyakarta.

blocks.name: Merapi slopes + Kaliurang
blocks.place: Lava trails and the 2010 eruption museum
see: Lava jeep tour and the Sisa Hartaku museum
Kaliurang forest walk
Ullen Sentalu Javanese culture museum

blocks.name: Bromo–Tengger
blocks.place: Sea of sand, crater rim, Penanjakan dawn viewpoint at 2,770 m
see: Dawn from Penanjakan or the quieter King Kong hill
Walk across the sand sea to the crater stairs
Cemoro Lawang village night
blocks.note: Iconic and packed at dawn. Dieng gives the same volcanic plateau without the jeep convoy.

blocks.name: Kawah Ijen
blocks.place: Night walk to the blue-flame crater, sulphur miners, turquoise lake
see: 2 am start, 1.5 h up, blue flames before dawn
Crater lake at sunrise
Coffee plantations on the way down
blocks.note: Hard on the lungs (gas masks provided); optional for Mom.

notes: Dry season across Java and South Sulawesi: 31°C and humid in the lowlands, 15–26°C in the highlands.
Toraja funeral ceremonies cluster in July and August, after the harvest.
Ramadan and Eid are in the first half of 2027, so no closures in this window.
Indonesian school holidays run to mid-July: Borobudur, Bromo and Yogyakarta are busiest before 18 July.

lodgingAssumption: Local B&B or Airbnb, two rooms for five, one meal out a day; shared van or hire car
